fields.justification: Stable identity is required for evidence and cross-reference integrity.
Classification makes completeness and policy checks deterministic.
The accepted or disputed meaning must remain explicit; only a change to this semantic unit can create a new requirement identity.
Required versus optional meaning controls terminal status, and required meaning cannot silently become optional.
Proposed, accepted, unresolved, disputed, unsupported, refused, and invalid meaning cannot be conflated.
Every accepted claim needs visible authority, and lower-ranked authority cannot silently override it.
No requirement may exist without attributable source evidence.
A requirement must map to planned test/evidence IDs proving its meaning, or record an explicit unresolved evidence obligation.
Consequential meaning invokes approval and fail-closed rules.
Approval evidence is conditional on consequential meaning and must be explicit, attributable, and scoped.
Default-derived meaning must identify the visible, attributable, authorized default record.
Stable source identity prevents silent evidence substitution.
Producer surfaces remain attributable while converging on one contract.
Byte-backed sources require content identity; ephemeral claims may lack bytes.
Current, missing, replaced, and withdrawn evidence have different validity; replacement links old and new source IDs without deleting old evidence.
A source assertion is evidence, not implicit authority.
Exact URI and JSON Pointer are preserved byte-for-byte and support reproducible diagnostics.
Every mapping record needs a stable, case-sensitive, unique identity.
A mapping is a machine-readable edge from a stable requirement identity to its outcome.
Direct, derived, defaulted, unresolved, prohibited, and missing representation are materially different.
Successful IR mappings must identify an exact RFC 6901 pointer into frozen IR v0.1.
Every authority/default decision behind a mapping must identify its controlling clause and evidence.
A mapping's validation evidence must be an immutable, content-addressable record.
Missing IR representation requires stable Phase 5 gap evidence.
Every top-level artifact declares the exact contract version.
Each validation attempt is a new immutable record with a stable identity.
Terminal outcomes must be explicit and machine-distinct.
The compile result is one of the explicit cross-referenced parts of the output boundary.
Non-success results carry sorted, machine-readable diagnostic references.
A result must reference the exact mapping records that name its accepted requirements and IR pointers.
The compile result references the evidence bundle that closes over its supporting records.
Stable sorted diagnostics explain non-success without prose parsing.
The evidence bundle needs a stable, unique identity like every other record.
The bundle must include the exact frozen IR target version its mappings validate against.
The evidence bundle closes over derivation records.
The evidence bundle closes over model-proposal records.
The evidence bundle closes over assumption records.
The evidence bundle closes over conflict records.
The evidence bundle closes over open-question records.
The evidence bundle closes over approval records.
The evidence bundle closes over default records.
The evidence bundle closes over planned test/evidence mapping records.
The evidence bundle closes over diagnostic records.
The evidence bundle closes over IR v0.1 gap records.
Every top-level artifact declares the exact contract version.
Evidence is content-addressable; the input digest anchors it to exact validated bytes.
The evidence bundle closes over the artifacts it validated.
Validation result must include every schema hash within the evidence bundle's closure.
The evidence bundle closes over the exact source evidence its accepted requirements reference.
Every requirement must appear in the bundle's mapping evidence.
The evidence bundle closes over the mapping records naming accepted requirements and IR pointers.
Validation evidence reports schema inventory/hashes, fixture outcomes, and determinism.
Contract validation must prove it did not access the network.
Contract validation must prove it did not read credentials.
